speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing dizziness, nausea, and imbalance; can you tell me if these symptoms started suddenly or developed gradually?

speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor

text: The audiometry and VEMP results are non-specific, so we need to determine the nature of your dizziness. Does the spinning sensation get worse when you change your head position, like looking up or rolling over in bed? Also, do you feel any pain behind your ears?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sustained sensation of the room spinning. I also have Occasional nausea, Use of diphenhydramine for symptoms and to aid sleep, Recent cold.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Persistent Postural-Perceptual Dizziness (PPPD). The sustained, constant spinning sensation without acute triggers like head movement or specific sounds, combined with a recent viral illness and lack of definitive Meniere's or SCD findings, is most consistent with this functional vestibular disorder.
